title: 08. Evaluation, Validation & Tuning: Hyperparameter Tuning
summary: Hyperparameter tuning is the process of finding the optimal hyperparameters for a machine learning model to achieve the best performance.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Hyperparameter tuning is the process of finding the optimal hyperparameters for a machine learning model to achieve the best performance. Hyperparameters are configuration settings that are set before training begins and cannot be learned from the data. Proper hyperparameter tuning can significantly improve model performance and is essential for building production-ready machine learning systems.

sections.title: What are Hyperparameters?
sections.body:
Hyperparameters are parameters that control the learning process and model architecture:

### Common Hyperparameters by Algorithm

#### 1. Linear Models
- **Regularization strength** (alpha, C, lambda)
- **Regularization type** (L1, L2, Elastic Net)
- **Learning rate** (for SGD)
- **Max iterations**

#### 2. Tree-Based Models
- **Number of trees** (n_estimators)
- **Maximum depth** (max_depth)
- **Minimum samples split** (min_samples_split)
- **Minimum samples leaf** (min_samples_leaf)
- **Maximum features** (max_features)
- **Subsample ratio** (subsample)

#### 3. Neural Networks
- **Number of layers** (n_layers)
- **Number of neurons per layer** (n_neurons)
- **Learning rate** (learning_rate)
- **Batch size** (batch_size)
- **Dropout rate** (dropout)
- **Activation functions** (activation)

#### 4. Support Vector Machines
- **Regularization parameter** (C)
- **Kernel type** (linear, rbf, poly)
- **Gamma** (kernel coefficient)
- **Degree** (for polynomial kernel)

#### 5. K-Nearest Neighbors
- **Number of neighbors** (n_neighbors)
- **Distance metric** (euclidean, manhattan, minkowski)
- **Weights** (uniform, distance)

sections.title: Hyperparameter Tuning Methods
sections.body:
### 1. Grid Search Cross-Validation

Grid search systematically tests all combinations of hyperparameters within a predefined grid.

#### How it Works
1. Define a grid of hyperparameter values
2. Train model for each combination
3. Evaluate using cross-validation
4. Select best performing combination

#### Advantages
- **Exhaustive**: Tests all combinations
- **Simple**: Easy to understand and implement
- **Deterministic**: Reproducible results

#### Disadvantages
- **Computationally expensive**: Scales exponentially with parameters
- **Inefficient**: May test poor combinations
- **Curse of dimensionality**: Becomes impractical with many parameters

#### When to Use
- Small number of hyperparameters
- Discrete parameter spaces
- When computational resources are available
- When you need exhaustive search

### 2. Random Search Cross-Validation

Random search randomly samples hyperparameter combinations from a defined space.

#### How it Works
1. Define parameter distributions
2. Randomly sample combinations
3. Train and evaluate each sample
4. Select best performing combination

#### Advantages
- **Efficient**: Often finds good solutions quickly
- **Scalable**: Works well with many parameters
- **Flexible**: Can handle continuous and discrete parameters

#### Disadvantages
- **Non-exhaustive**: May miss optimal combinations
- **Random**: Results may vary between runs
- **No guarantee**: No guarantee of finding global optimum

#### When to Use
- Many hyperparameters
- Limited computational resources
- When approximate solutions are acceptable
- Continuous parameter spaces

### 3. Bayesian Optimization

Bayesian optimization uses probabilistic models to predict which hyperparameter combinations are most likely to improve performance.

#### How it Works
1. Build probabilistic model of objective function
2. Use acquisition function to select next point
3. Evaluate selected point
4. Update model and repeat

#### Key Components

##### Surrogate Model
- **Gaussian Process**: Most common choice
- **Random Forest**: Good for discrete parameters
- **Tree-structured Parzen Estimators (TPE)**: Efficient for many parameters

##### Acquisition Function
- **Expected Improvement (EI)**: Balances exploration and exploitation
- **Upper Confidence Bound (UCB)**: Emphasizes exploration
- **Probability of Improvement (PI)**: Conservative approach

#### Advantages
- **Efficient**: Requires fewer evaluations
- **Intelligent**: Learns from previous evaluations
- **Handles noise**: Robust to evaluation noise
- **Scalable**: Works well with many parameters

#### Disadvantages
- **Complex**: More difficult to implement
- **Computational overhead**: Model fitting adds cost
- **Hyperparameters**: Optimization itself has parameters

#### When to Use
- Expensive objective functions
- Many hyperparameters
- Limited evaluation budget
- When efficiency is crucial

### 4. Manual Hyperparameter Tuning

Manual tuning involves systematically adjusting hyperparameters based on domain knowledge and experimentation.

#### Techniques

##### Learning Curves
- Plot training and validation performance vs. hyperparameter
- Identify overfitting and underfitting
- Find sweet spot between bias and variance

##### Sensitivity Analysis
- Test one parameter at a time
- Understand parameter impact
- Identify most important parameters

##### Domain Knowledge
- Use prior experience
- Apply theoretical understanding
- Consider problem characteristics

#### Advantages
- **Interpretable**: Understand parameter effects
- **Efficient**: Focus on important parameters
- **Flexible**: Can adapt to specific problems

#### Disadvantages
- **Subjective**: Depends on expertise
- **Time-consuming**: Requires manual effort
- **Limited**: May miss optimal combinations

#### When to Use
- Limited computational resources
- When interpretability is important
- When you have domain expertise
- For initial exploration

sections.title: Advanced Optimization Libraries
sections.body:
### 1. Optuna

Optuna is a hyperparameter optimization framework that supports various optimization algorithms.

#### Features
- **Multiple samplers**: TPE, Random, Grid, CMA-ES
- **Pruning**: Early stopping of unpromising trials
- **Visualization**: Study analysis and plotting
- **Distributed optimization**: Parallel execution

#### Key Concepts
- **Study**: Optimization session
- **Trial**: Single hyperparameter evaluation
- **Sampler**: Strategy for selecting parameters
- **Pruner**: Strategy for stopping trials early

### 2. Hyperopt

Hyperopt is a Python library for serial and parallel optimization over awkward search spaces.

#### Features
- **Multiple algorithms**: TPE, Random, Annealing
- **Flexible spaces**: Real, integer, categorical
- **Parallel execution**: MongoDB integration
- **Bayesian optimization**: Tree-structured Parzen estimators

#### Key Concepts
- **Search space**: Define parameter distributions
- **Objective function**: Function to minimize
- **Trials**: Database of evaluations
- **Fmin**: Main optimization function

### 3. Scikit-Optimize

Scikit-optimize is a library for sequential model-based optimization.

#### Features
- **Gaussian processes**: Surrogate modeling
- **Multiple acquisition functions**: EI, LCB, PI
- **Visualization**: Optimization progress
- **Integration**: Works with scikit-learn

sections.title: Best Practices
sections.body:
### 1. Define Search Space

#### Parameter Ranges
- **Log-scale**: For learning rates, regularization
- **Linear scale**: For counts, sizes
- **Categorical**: For algorithm choices

#### Constraints
- **Dependencies**: Some parameters depend on others
- **Bounds**: Physical or logical constraints
- **Discrete vs. Continuous**: Choose appropriate representations

### 2. Choose Evaluation Metric

#### Considerations
- **Business objective**: Align with goals
- **Robustness**: Use cross-validation
- **Interpretability**: Choose meaningful metrics
- **Balance**: Consider multiple metrics

#### Common Choices
- **Regression**: RMSE, MAE, R²
- **Classification**: Accuracy, F1-score, ROC-AUC
- **Ranking**: NDCG, MAP, Precision@k

### 3. Implement Cross-Validation

#### Types
- **K-fold**: Standard approach
- **Stratified**: For imbalanced data
- **Time series**: For temporal data
- **Nested**: For unbiased estimates

#### Considerations
- **Stability**: Multiple runs for consistency
- **Computational cost**: Balance with accuracy
- **Data leakage**: Avoid information leakage

### 4. Handle Computational Constraints

#### Strategies
- **Early stopping**: Stop unpromising trials
- **Resource allocation**: Distribute resources efficiently
- **Parallelization**: Use multiple cores/machines
- **Pruning**: Eliminate poor candidates early

### 5. Monitor and Analyze

#### Tracking
- **Progress**: Monitor optimization progress
- **Convergence**: Check if optimization converged
- **Overfitting**: Watch for overfitting to validation set

#### Analysis
- **Parameter importance**: Understand which parameters matter
- **Interactions**: Look for parameter interactions
- **Sensitivity**: Analyze parameter sensitivity

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
### 1. Overfitting to Validation Set

#### Problem
- Optimizing too many hyperparameters
- Using same validation set repeatedly
- Not using nested cross-validation

#### Solutions
- Limit number of hyperparameters
- Use separate test set
- Implement nested cross-validation

### 2. Insufficient Search

#### Problem
- Too few trials
- Poor search space definition
- Inadequate optimization time

#### Solutions
- Allocate sufficient computational budget
- Define appropriate search spaces
- Use efficient optimization algorithms

### 3. Ignoring Parameter Interactions

#### Problem
- Optimizing parameters independently
- Missing important interactions
- Suboptimal solutions

#### Solutions
- Use joint optimization
- Consider parameter dependencies
- Analyze interaction effects

### 4. Not Considering Uncertainty

#### Problem
- Single evaluation per configuration
- Ignoring evaluation noise
- Overconfident in results

#### Solutions
- Multiple evaluations per configuration
- Account for evaluation uncertainty
- Use robust optimization methods
